tags.name: Organizations API
tags.description:
The Organizations API allows you to manage organizations, or tenants. Organizations are separate entities and are managed independently. Each organization has its own resources, in isolation from other organizations.

As a service provider, you can use the Organizations API to manage your customers' organizations. As an organization owner, you can use the Organizations API to manage your organization's resources.

tags.name: Users API
tags.description:
The Users API allows you to manage users, of whom are members of organizations. Users are associated with Authentication Providers, which are used to authenticate users. Multiple Authentication Providers can be associated with a single user.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is supported and can be enabled for individual users.

tags.name: Datacenters API
tags.description:
The Datacenters API allows you to manage datacenters, which are logical groups of clusters. Datacenters are typically located in various geographical locations.

In order to reduce latency when Pextra CloudEnvironment is deployed across multiple datacenters, it is recommended to set datacenter locations. This will allow Pextra CloudEnvironment to automatically optimize latency when internally routing requests.

tags.name: Clusters API
tags.description:
The Clusters API allows you to manage clusters, which are groups of nodes. It is strongly recommended to configure cluster nodes in a manner that ensures low-latency connections between them.

Nodes owned by separate organizations should not be part of the same cluster. Clusters are used to manage the distribution of workloads across nodes, and therefore, mixing nodes from different organizations is not recommended.

tags.name: Nodes API
tags.description:
The Nodes API allows you to manage nodes, which are servers that run Pextra CloudEnvironment. Nodes are part of clusters, and are used to deploy Instances.

Clusters with one node are running in standalone mode, and are not recommended for production use.

tags.name: Volumes API
tags.description:
The Volumes API allows you to manage volumes, which are virtual storage devices that can be attached to instances. Volumes are allocated from storage pools, stored on individual nodes, and are used to store data.

Volumes can be attached to instances to provide additional storage capacity. Volumes can be resized, detached, and destroyed as needed. To attach or detach a volume, use the Instances API.

tags.name: Instances API
tags.description:
The Instances API allows you to manage Instances, which are virtualized applications or operating systems. Instances are deployed on nodes within clusters.

There are currently four types of Instances:
- Docker (fast, lightweight containers, worst isolation/security)
- Podman (fast, lightweight containers, good isolation/security)
- QEMU Virtual Machines (slow, heavy virtual machines, best isolation/security)
- LXC Containers (fast, lightweight containers, good isolation/security)

tags.name: Custom Jobs API
tags.description:
**Note**: Internally, custom jobs are referred to as 'instance jobs', but they are not necessarily associated with instances. This is due to an early design decision that has not been changed for backwards compatibility reasons.

The Custom Jobs API allows you to manage custom jobs, which are user-defined jobs that are performed on a regular schedule. Custom jobs are defined on the cluster level, and can be associated with multiple nodes, depending on the job type. Custom jobs can be used to perform operations such as backups and other maintenance tasks, on one or more nodes in a cluster.

Custom jobs can be scheduled to run at specific times, or can be run on demand. Custom jobs that are already running at the scheduled time will not be executed again if the scheduling interval is not met. This means that if a job is scheduled to run every 5 minutes, and it is already running at the 5 minute mark, it will not be executed again until the next 5 minute mark.

It is strongly recommended to use a scheduling interval of at least 30 minutes for custom jobs, to avoid overloading nodes. This is especially important for resource-intensive jobs, such as backups. The minimum scheduling interval is 5 minutes, but it is not recommended to use it for production workloads.

tags.name: Networking API
tags.description:
The Networking API allows you to manage networking resources, such as vSwitches and vSwitch Port Groups. vSwitches are virtualized network switches.

There are two types of vSwitches:
- Standalone vSwitches: vSwitches that are managed by a single node.
- Distributed vSwitches: vSwitches that are managed by a cluster.

vSwitch Port Groups are logical groups of network interfaces that are used to connect instances to vSwitches. vSwitch Port Groups can have firewall rules and other configuration settings, such as VLANs, trunking, and more.

- System keys: These are keys that are stored on this node.
- Authorized keys: These are keys that are stored on other nodes in the cluster, but are authorized for this node.

For security reasons, private keys are not included in the response.

This endpoint uploads an instance image to a storage pool on a node. The image can be used to deploy instances on the node.

The image must be in a supported format by the respective instance type.

- Docker/Podman: .tar
- LXC: .tar.gz, .tar.xz

- Images will not be tagged with the `name` field; the image will be tagged with the tag present in the image.

Note that a malicious image can compromise the node. Ensure that the image is from a trusted source.
